name: INWI Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: Awarded from the founding tournament's own final on 23 March 1997 (Pimp Daddy Brown over John Stillwater), the top prize churned through four champions across the year -- Brown to Brody Thunder at SuperCard I's Steel Cage main event, Thunder to the Springer in the 1997 Ringmaster PPV main event, and the Springer to Tony Houston by the following show, Houston still champion at Winter Storm '97.

name: INWI United States Championship

events.title: inwi-new-york
events.note: Renamed on-air to the New York Championship; same belt, same lineage (Sam Adams was champion through the rename).

epitaph: Crowned in the same 23 March tournament final (Jason Starr over PO Box), the belt passed through John Stillwater and PO Box before Mike Garvey took it at Heat Wave '97; renamed on-air to the New York Championship around mid-October under its reigning champion, Sam Adams, with the lineage carried unbroken under its new name (see inwi-new-york).

name: INWI Television Championship
epitaph: Won in the founding tournament final by Vito Rizzotto, the belt changed hands to Mr. Apples within days and stayed with him for the bulk of the spring and summer before a fast rotation through Harvey Thunder, Ultimate Perversion, Pig Pen and Jason Chandler carried it to year's end.

name: INWI Northeast Television Championship
epitaph: One of two Northeast-branded belts awarded the same tournament weekend (23 March), crowned on Brody Thunder before a run of short reigns -- the Springer, Mike Garvey, Firestar, Vito Rizzotto, Bill Bob Woijicowski -- settled with Tony Houston from mid-August on.

name: INWI Northeast Championship
epitaph: The other Northeast-branded belt from the founding weekend (Jonathan Sunset), its lineage is the wing's most volatile: it passed through Brody Thunder, a vacancy-filling battle royal (Mr. Ed Rogers), Dell Pickle, Zack Sharp, the Springer (twice, trading with Sharp), Rogers again, King Apples, and finally Bill Bob Woijicowski, who won it at Winter Storm '97 wrestling in disguise as a mystery entrant.

name: INWI Tag Team Championship
epitaph: The founding tournament's tag final (23 March) crowned the MacDaddies as the first Heavyweight Tag Team Champions; the Big Brothers, the Terminators, the Comforters and, at year's end, the ad hoc pairing of James Pillow and Vinny Vitrone all held it before the returning Friendship Express -- disguised as 'the Masks' -- won it at Winter Storm '97.

name: INWI TV Tag Team Championship
epitaph: The consolation half of the founding tag final (the Peeler Brothers), this belt bounced hardest of all -- the Friendship Express and Solid Gold traded it repeatedly across the spring and summer before Solid Gold's own reign from mid-July ran uninterrupted through the rest of the wing's own served record.

name: INWI Light Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: Introduced mid-year and awarded by its own tournament final at Heat Wave '97 (Sam Adams over David McCarter), the belt passed through Awesome X and McCarter again before a late-year stretch (James Pillow, Bill Bob Woijicowski) ended with Michael Bane holding it into December.

name: INWI Ringmaster
epitaph: A summer-long single-elimination tournament with its own belt, trophy and kayfabe cash purse, culminating in a PPV final; "Cold and Calculating" Tony Houston beat Jason Chandler to become the first-ever Ringmaster at the fed's own 1997 Ringmaster PPV. The '1997' in its own name implies annual intent, though no second edition survives in this wing's own holdings.

name: INWI New York Championship
notes: The United States Championship, renamed on-air in October 1997; the reign ledger continues unbroken under Sam Adams.
epitaph: The United States Championship's own lineage continues here under its on-air rename (see inwi-united-states); Sam Adams carried it through the autumn before Mr. Cherry won it at Winter Storm '97.

name: INWI Trans-Atlantic Championship
epitaph: Introduced by 1999 as a successor to an earlier, unheld "Can-Am" belt; Jeffrey Drake held it into the promotion's own closing weekend before losing it to Kris Klepan on the second night, 20 March 1999.

name: FWA World Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: A second world-level belt contested on the promotion's own closing weekend under different branding from the promotion's own name; its own promotional origin is not explained in the surviving text. Mr. Apples defended it against Brody Thunder in a taped-fist ladder match on the promotion's first closing night, 19 March 1999, and lost it.
